papers.title: NP-Hardness of Approximating Meta-Complexity: A Cryptographic Approach
papers.abstract: It is a longstanding open problem whether the Minimum Circuit Size Problem (MCSP) and related meta-complexity problems are NP-complete and hard to approximate. In this work, we show that under plausible cryptographic assumptions, the problem of approximating the circuit complexity of a truth table is NP-hard. Our approach uses a novel connection between meta-complexity and the security of pseudorandom generators. We develop a framework for reducing approximation problems in meta-complexity to cryptographic hardness assumptions, yielding the first hardness results for approximating MCSP. Our results also have implications for the complexity of learning and the existence of one-way functions.
